name: Creamy Coleslaw
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt writes that he came to coleslaw late, after a bad KFC encounter and a much better tangy, barely-creamy version at a Boston restaurant, and this is his attempt at that lightly dressed style. He argues green cabbage beats savoy because its crunch and sulfurous bite hold up, and that the cabbage must be pre-treated or the dressed salad turns watery and raw-tasting. His testing showed that a heavy salt-and-sugar coating draws out moisture fast, so a five-minute purge followed by a cold rinse concentrates flavor without wrecking texture, while longer sits make the shreds limp. He also found that blotting or salad-spinning the rinsed vegetables dry, rather than wringing them out, preserves the crunch, and that the concentrated cabbage then needs only a small amount of mayonnaise-cider vinegar-Dijon dressing plus far more black pepper than seems sensible.
comment_digest: The dominant complaint is salt. Several cooks found the half-cup of kosher salt overwhelming and blamed volume measurement: one notes Kenji almost certainly used Diamond Crystal and reports using 68.5 g for Morton's with good results; another had to soak the vegetables in water to undo the damage; others ask outright for gram weights, and one long review criticizes the recipe for giving no weights at all. Repeat advice: rinse very thoroughly and taste the vegetables after rinsing to confirm they are bland before dressing, since under-rinsing has ruined batches. Celery seed is a popular addition, mentioned by more than one reviewer. One halved the vegetables (1.5 lb cabbage before coring) and still had dressing left over, suggesting the dressing yield runs generous. Another halves the black pepper. Unanswered questions include whether bagged slaw mix needs the purge and whether 3.5 lb of cabbage is really correct.
flags: Manifest calls this 'Creamy Coleslaw' but the page title is 'Classic Coleslaw' (URL slug is creamy-cole-slaw) - same recipe, different title. Recipe gives no weights for the salt/sugar purge, which multiple reviewers flag as a real problem; Kenji's own reply confirms a 2013 vintage. Several reviewer comments end in 'Read More' and may be truncated.
